status_policy.promotion_policy: A rule is never promoted from proposal or committee review to adopted, in-force or applicable by model inference. Adoption, entry into force and application dates remain separate. A rule's jurisdiction, vessel scope, voyage scope and reporting period must be resolved for each case.
limitations: This snapshot is a research register, not legal advice or a verifier determination.
Official meeting summaries can evidence committee decisions but do not replace the adopted legal text or charted geographic boundary.
Re-fetch and review official instruments before every real reporting period; this dated snapshot must not be treated as timeless.

rules.title: IMO phase-two review of EEXI, SEEMP and CII short-term GHG measures
rules.instrument: MEPC 84 outcome and intersessional work plan

applicability.ship_scope: Ships within the scope of the relevant IMO short-term GHG measures; vessel-specific applicability remains subject to current MARPOL/IMO instruments.
applicability.geographic_scope: International shipping under applicable IMO instruments.
applicability.voyage_scope: Design and annual operational efficiency metrics; route and reporting boundaries depend on the underlying measure.
conditions: Phase-two review includes possible revisions to EEXI, SEEMP and CII measures and consideration of wind propulsion in EEDI/EEXI calculations.
exclusions_or_unknowns: No new WAPS credit formula is established by the review workplan.
Do not treat candidate amendments as current legal requirements.

limitations: This is a review/workplan, not an adopted wind-propulsion credit formula or vessel-specific statutory calculation.

rules.title: Marine diesel engine CH4/N2O measurement and calculation guidelines

applicability.ship_scope: Marine diesel engines and relevant test-bed/onboard measurement programmes, subject to each resolution's detailed scope.
applicability.voyage_scope: Tank-to-wake CH4 and/or N2O measurement and calculation.
conditions: MEPC.414(84) addresses test-bed/onboard measurements.
MEPC.415(84) addresses engine-load monitoring and calculation of emission values.
MEPC.416(84) addresses continuous emission monitoring systems.
exclusions_or_unknowns: Do not assume measurement data exists unless suitable calibrated instruments and records are available.
Confirm mandatory/voluntary status and applicable method from the resolution and current IMO instructions.

limitations: Guidelines do not establish that a particular ship's instruments are calibrated or that emissions records have been independently verified.

rules.title: EU Emissions Trading System maritime transport coverage
rules.instrument: Directive 2003/87/EC as amended, including Directive (EU) 2023/959 and maritime implementing provisions
rules.revision_or_resolution: Consolidated text and current Commission guidance must be consulted

applicability.ship_scope: Since 2024: cargo and passenger ships ≥5,000 GT; from 2027: offshore ships ≥5,000 GT. MRV scope differs and includes additional 400–5,000 GT offshore/general cargo ships from 2025.
applicability.geographic_scope: EU/EEA port emissions and voyages with EU port calls, as defined in current law.
applicability.voyage_scope: 100% coverage for voyages between EU ports and emissions within EU ports; 50% coverage for voyages with one end outside the EU, subject to the legal rules.
conditions: The EU ETS is flag-neutral and route-based.
100% of emissions for eligible voyages between EU/EEA ports and 100% of eligible emissions within EU/EEA ports.
50% of eligible emissions for voyages between an EU/EEA port and a non-EU/EEA port.
CH4 and N2O are included in ETS maritime scope from emissions year 2026.
exclusions_or_unknowns: Applicability, responsible company, ship scope, exemptions and voyage classification must be resolved from legal text and verified facts.

output_scope: EU ETS covered CH4 emissions from 2026
EU ETS covered N2O emissions from 2026

calculation_contract.formula_or_method: Aggregate gas-specific emissions by eligible voyage/port segment and reporting year, applying the legally defined coverage share and surrender phase-in. Preserve each gas and the applicable GWP/calculation method.

surrender_phase_in.meaning: 40% of emissions from 2024 to be covered by allowances surrendered in 2025.
70% of emissions from 2025 to be covered by allowances surrendered in 2026.
100% of emissions from 2026 to be covered by allowances surrendered in 2027; full surrender applies thereafter under current rules.

voyage_coverage.voyage_scope: Voyage departing an EU/EEA Member State port and arriving at an EU/EEA Member State port.
voyage_coverage.emissions_boundary: All emissions of the eligible voyage, with within-port emissions accounted separately according to the regulation.
limitations: Subject to port-call definition, derogations and applicable ship/company scope.

voyage_coverage.voyage_scope: Voyage departing an EU/EEA Member State port and arriving outside EU/EEA jurisdiction.
voyage_coverage.emissions_boundary: Half of the eligible voyage emissions.
limitations: Subject to legally defined port-of-call rules and derogations.

voyage_coverage.voyage_scope: Voyage departing outside EU/EEA jurisdiction and arriving at an EU/EEA Member State port.
voyage_coverage.emissions_boundary: Half of the eligible voyage emissions.
limitations: Subject to legally defined port-of-call rules and derogations.

voyage_coverage.voyage_scope: Emissions within a qualifying EU/EEA port of call.
voyage_coverage.emissions_boundary: Emissions at berth and ship movements within port limits, counted without duplication with voyage emissions.
limitations: Port approach/departure outside port of call is part of the voyage, not within-port emissions.
Verify ship/reporting scope under applicable law.
Gas enters EU ETS maritime scope from 2026; MRV monitoring/reporting scope began earlier.
Gas enters EU ETS maritime scope from 2026; MRV monitoring/reporting scope began earlier.
Surrender phase-in is not the same as the geographic covered-emissions fraction.
Do not apply one fleet-wide coverage ratio to every voyage or period.

rules.title: EU Monitoring, Reporting and Verification of maritime transport emissions
rules.revision_or_resolution: Consolidated EU MRV Maritime Regulation and applicable implementing acts

applicability.ship_scope: From 2024: cargo and passenger ships ≥5,000 GT; from 2025 reporting period: offshore ships ≥5,000 GT and offshore/general cargo ships ≥400 GT and <5,000 GT, subject to detailed legal scope and exclusions.
applicability.geographic_scope: Voyages to, from and between EU/EEA ports and emissions within ports under the MRV Maritime Regulation's scope.
applicability.voyage_scope: Monitoring, reporting and verification of gas-specific ship emissions and related activity data for each reporting period; do not confuse the MRV scope with EU ETS allowance coverage.
conditions: CO2 has been monitored/reported under EU MRV since 2018.
CH4 and N2O are within EU MRV monitoring/reporting from emissions year 2024.
Annual reporting follows the statutory reporting period and voyage/port definitions.
exclusions_or_unknowns: Exact ship scope, monitoring plan, port-call definition, exclusions and verifier requirements must be resolved under the consolidated regulation and implementing acts.
MRV reporting coverage does not mean all reported gases are in EU ETS surrender scope in the same year.

calculation_contract.formula_or_method: Monitor and aggregate ship emissions and activity data using the prescribed MRV monitoring plan and approved method. Preserve CO2, CH4 and N2O as separate gases and bind to the relevant reporting year and verifier status.

limitations: Subject to ship and reporting scope under the regulation.
Gas included in the MRV monitoring/reporting scope from 2024.
Gas included in the MRV monitoring/reporting scope from 2024.
MRV is a monitoring/reporting/verification obligation, not an allowance surrender requirement.
MRV gas coverage and EU ETS gas coverage have different start years; do not reuse one rule for both.

rules.title: FuelEU Maritime annual well-to-wake GHG intensity requirement
rules.revision_or_resolution: Use consolidated Regulation and applicable delegated/implementing acts

applicability.ship_scope: Ships and energy use within FuelEU Maritime's vessel, size, company and voyage scope.
applicability.geographic_scope: EU/EEA port and voyage scope as defined in Regulation (EU) 2023/1805.
applicability.voyage_scope: Annual average GHG intensity of energy used on board under the Regulation's well-to-wake boundary.
conditions: Reference GHG intensity is 91.16 gCO2e/MJ.
The regulation defines yearly reduction factors and specific treatment of eligible fuels/flexibilities.
exclusions_or_unknowns: Verify RFNBO reward, banking, borrowing, pooling, exemptions and verification under current text and acts.
A generic tank-to-wake CO2 factor is not a substitute.

calculation_contract.formula_or_method: Calculate annual average well-to-wake GHG intensity of energy used on board using the prescribed fuel pathway, gas and GWP methodology, then compare with the applicable target after reduction factor.

limitations: A regulation calculation is not a verifier statement; all ship scope, fuel pathway and annual energy records must be evidenced.

rules.title: North-East Atlantic Emission Control Area
rules.instrument: MARPOL Annex VI amendment adopted at MEPC 84

applicability.ship_scope: Ships subject to MARPOL Annex VI sulphur requirements while operating within the designated ECA.
applicability.geographic_scope: Exclusive economic zones and territorial seas extending up to 200 nautical miles from baselines of Greenland, Iceland, the Faroe Islands, Ireland, the mainland United Kingdom, France, Spain and Portugal, as described in the MEPC 84 outcome; authoritative adopted coordinates/chart data are still required.
applicability.voyage_scope: Voyage legs and port/operational segments within the ECA after the effective application date.
conditions: The ECA enters into force on 1 September 2027 and takes effect 12 months later, on 1 September 2028.
Within ECAs, fuel sulphur content must not exceed 0.10%.
The adopted North-East Atlantic ECA establishes additional NOx, SOx and particulate matter emission-control requirements.
exclusions_or_unknowns: Exact implementation date and charted coordinates must be read from the adopted MARPOL amendment and official charts.
This is a local air-pollution requirement, not a WtW GHG factor.

limitations: Adoption is distinct from application; route geometry alone does not establish fuel compliance.

rules.title: EU ETS Directive targeted revision proposal — COM(2026) 616
rules.instrument: Proposal for a Directive amending Directive 2003/87/EC and Decision (EU) 2015/1814

applicability.ship_scope: Proposed changes to the EU ETS Directive including targeted maritime scope and offshore-operation provisions; exact ship categories and thresholds remain subject to legislative adoption.
applicability.geographic_scope: EU ETS jurisdiction as defined by the final Directive.
applicability.voyage_scope: Scenario analysis only; current EU ETS voyage coverage and surrender duties are not changed by this proposal.
conditions: Legislative proposal would extend EU ETS/MRV coverage to certain additional categories of ships to reinforce the level playing field.
Proposal includes tailored safeguards against evasion by vessels performing or supporting offshore operations.
Proposal includes review provisions concerning international IMO measures and interactions with ETS scope and double-payment risk.
exclusions_or_unknowns: European Parliament procedure 2026/0212(COD) status is awaiting committee decision in the 10 November 2026 snapshot.
This proposal is not adopted law and must not alter current ETS liabilities.
Final ship scope, offshore definitions, reporting periods, exemptions and application dates depend on the adopted text.

limitations: Proposal published 17 July 2026; refresh after later parliamentary/Council decisions.
Do not treat proposed provisions as binding or applicable.

rules.title: Maritime MRV and FuelEU streamlining proposal — COM(2026) 620
rules.instrument: Proposal for a Regulation amending Regulations (EU) 2015/757 and (EU) 2023/1805

applicability.ship_scope: Proposed changes to maritime MRV and FuelEU monitoring/reporting; proposal would extend MRV to additional ship categories including oil/chemical/gas/LNG tankers, Ro-Pax and passenger ships 400–5,000 GT from 2029, subject to final text.
applicability.geographic_scope: EU/EEA maritime MRV and FuelEU scope as defined by adopted legislation.
applicability.voyage_scope: Scenario analysis only until the regulation is adopted and applicable.
conditions: Proposal seeks one aligned MRV system for GHG emissions, well-to-wake emissions and energy used on board, with a single monitoring plan and a single ship report.
Proposed definition of energy used on board is GJ for propulsion and onboard equipment at sea or at berth.
Proposed substitute energy sources include renewable energy generated on board, onshore power supply and wind-assisted propulsion systems.
Proposed definition of wind-assisted propulsion includes partial or full propulsion by wind energy harnessed through rotor sails, kites, hard/rigid sails, soft sails, suction wings or turbines.

Proposed monitoring method counts fuel use from all fuel consumers and energy from substitute sources; wind energy amount is to use international standards and certification references specified in future Commission implementing acts.
Proposal text requires transparent, reproducible monitoring records and proposes at least 10 years of data retention.
exclusions_or_unknowns: European Parliament procedure 2026/0210(COD) status is awaiting committee decision in the 10 November 2026 snapshot.
The proposal itself does not specify the wind-energy calculation standard/certification method; future implementing acts are contemplated.
This is not an adopted rule and does not establish a current legal WAPS energy-accounting formula.
Do not equate modelled avoided fuel or shaft-energy displacement with regulatory wind-energy-used values without the future method.

limitations: Proposal published 17 July 2026; refresh as the ordinary legislative procedure progresses.
Standards/certification for wind-energy amount are future implementing acts and are not supplied by this record.
Do not infer that the proposal or its future methodology is in force.
